yaml.route: Narrow the core by effective results only: Yamada 2020 Thm 1.1 (PR #1172), then on its remainder an elementary prime-interval separation with the prime-gap theorems of Nagura 1952 and Schoenfeld 1976 as cited holes.
yaml.detail: Only an effective result with explicit constants can narrow a statement whose remaining cases are concrete (n > 10^6, value > 10^60). Ineffective results cannot: a hole 'there is T such that collisions of value ≥ T have shape X' leaves a remainder that must hold for every T, which is the core again. That rules out Siegel/Beukers–Shorey–Tijdeman per-pair finiteness, Brindza's superelliptic finiteness and MRSTT 2022 Thm 1.3 ('t sufficiently large') as narrowings here. Effective inputs used on 2026-10-29: (1) Yamada, arXiv:2002.07043, Thm 1.1, for N ≥ 500000 in the window M < K < N/2, M ≤ 0.735K (a preprint); (2) the elementary fact, proved in Lean, that a prime p with max(m, n−k) < p ≤ n divides C(n,k) and not C(m,l); with Nagura (prime in (x, 6x/5), x ≥ 25) and Schoenfeld (prime in (x, x + x/16597), x ≥ 2010759.9) this leaves only collisions with m > 16597n/16598 or k < n/16598 once n > 4021520 (m > 5n/6 or k < n/6 for n > 10^6). Sharper explicit gaps (Dusart 2010 Prop 6.8: (x, x(1 + 1/(25 ln² x))] for x ≥ 396738) would push this to m > n(1 − 1/(25 ln² n)) or k < n/(25 ln² n), with real logarithms in the statement. Nothing found bounds l in terms of k, and nothing effective treats m close to n with k small, which is where the remaining core now lives.

yaml.route: Clear denominators: C(n,k) = C(n−1,k+2) is exactly the cubic (39) of Stroeker–de Weger 1999 at (u,v) = (k,n); assembly proved (PR #1166), hole = their Theorem 3.
yaml.detail: The remaining hole --h1 is Stroeker–de Weger 1999 Theorem 3 (all integral points of (39), a rank-1 elliptic curve). Its proof is a linear form in elliptic logarithms (David's bound) plus LLL reduction. Nothing in Mathlib formalises integral points on elliptic curves, and no elementary argument is known to me: (39) has real points along an asymptote of irrational slope (the real root of t³ + t² − 1 = 0 governs k/(n−k)), so congruence or size arguments alone do not close it. Numerically no integral point beyond the eight with |u|,|v| < 2000 (C) and none with n−k−2 < 300000 (A).
